sources.title: Ernst Hairer, Syvert P. Nørsett, and Gerhard Wanner, Solving Ordinary Differential Equations I: Nonstiff Problems, 2nd ed., Springer (corrected printing)
sources.locator: Chapter III.5, Variable Step Size Multistep Methods, printed pp. 397–409 (PDF pp. 408–420), including actual-node Adams interpolation and variable-step BDF2 formula/stability/convergence; the PECE implementation passage is §III.7, printed pp. 423–424 (PDF pp. 434–435).

contents.name: §III.5, pp. 397–400: variable-step Adams formulas from interpolation at actual nodes and integration
contents.support: The source constructs variable-step Adams formulas by interpolating derivative values at the actual past nodes and integrating the polynomial; the carrier gives the complete Lagrange-basis formula and proof.

contents.name: §III.5, pp. 400–401: BDF derivative interpolation, variable-step BDF2 coefficients, and order convention
contents.support: The source derives variable-step BDF by differentiating the solution interpolant and gives the BDF2 ratio formula; the carrier independently differentiates the quadratic Lagrange basis and proves its cubic residual.

contents.name: §III.5, pp. 402–406: variable-step BDF2 stability and the 1+sqrt(2) ratio boundary
contents.support: The source identifies the BDF2 parasitic factor and its ratio threshold. The carrier derives q(r)=r^2/(1+2r) and proves the strict uniform contraction used downstream; the source’s broader companion-product argument is not substituted for that local proof.

contents.name: §III.5, pp. 407–409: variable-step consistency, bounded coefficients, and convergence error propagation
contents.support: The source derives global error propagation from stability, local defect, bounded coefficients, and accurate starts. The carrier supplies its own forced first-difference estimate, branch assumptions, and complete O(H^2) proof.

contents.name: §III.7, pp. 423–424: DEABM predictor-evaluate-correct-evaluate implementation
contents.support: The source explicitly gives P-E-C-E order and the final corrected-state evaluation for the next step; the local algorithm specifies these operations and its failure statuses.

contents.name: §III.7, pp. 423–424: one corrector iteration compared with solving the implicit Adams equation
contents.support: The source describes one corrector iteration; the exact scalar stability-factor comparison is independently proved in the example.
